newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed, USDA data weighs on futures.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed, USDA data weighs on futures.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed amid bearish input from USDA's December supply/demand report and weekly export sales report, traders said.
"Exports on everything were healthy except for corn," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

USDA Thursday said net export sales of corn for the week ended December 5 totaled 507,900 tonnes. That tally was above expectations but below the weekly level needed to "turn bullish heads," a trader said.
USDA Thursday increased slightly its outlook for 1996-97 U.S. corn carryover.
The government said on August 31, 1997 the U.S. corn supply would total 1.157 billion bushels, above the 1.107 billion it predicted in its November supply/demand data.
Corn was underpinned by a rally in wheat and soybeans with gains in the livestock sector also cited.
"Look at meat prices. They're up so we're going to expand herds eventually which is bullish for corn," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Corn closed 1/4 cent per bushel lower to 2-1/2 higher, with December up 1/4 at $2.67-3/4.

Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of March and Smith Barney bought 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said. E.D. and F. Man International sold two million bushels of March and Farmers Commodities Corp sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 43,000 contracts, above the 42,577 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Smith Barney bought 3,000 December $3.30 calls and sold 2,000 December $2.40 puts, traders said. The firm also bought 1,600 December puts and sold 2,400 December $3.20 calls, the traders said, and USA Trading bought 1,000 December $3.20 calls, sold 1,000 December $2.60 calls and sold 370 December $4.40 puts.
Corn options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, above the 10,540 traded Wednesday.
